messages:
Priya (Growth PM): Heads-up: planning a small production test next Wed to compare a compact banded-pricing widget (badges for Typical, Peak, Enterprise) vs the existing tier page. Goal: measure demo requests and FAQ engagement. Who's available for a quick sync?
Sam (UX): I can join. Are we keeping the full tier copy in variant B or trimming it?
Priya (Growth PM): Variant A (badges): microcopy, inline tooltip FAQ popovers, commitment badge that shows 'Est. monthly' after input. Variant B (full): expanded tier sections + accordion FAQ. Trim language on A to reduce reading time.
Elaine (Content): I'll write 3 badge labels: "Typical", "Peak", "Enterprise-grade". Also draft two FAQ styles: popover snippets (~30 chars) and accordion answers (~120 chars). Anything to avoid in the popover?
Sam (UX): Keep popover non-modal and accessible. Use keyboard-focus and ESC to close. Also add a small benchmark line beneath badges: "Median p95 latency ~75ms on Dedicated" 12; use lightweight typography.
Marcos (Design): I'll mock the badge layout and a compact tooltip arrow. Suggest color scheme: muted teal for Typical, amber for Peak, deep blue for Enterprise.
Jordan (RevOps): Routing note: any demo request from Variant A with "Enterprise-grade" selected should be flagged as high-touch. Add tag: pricing_expt=banded_enterprise. Also for Variant B, if accordion faq opens >2 times and form is started, route to SDR.
Alex (Analytics): Tracking: create GA event "pricing_badge_select" and "faq_popover_open". We'll use experiment id pricing_band_v_full_2026_04_01. I'll set up segmentation for referral and first-touch. ETA: instrument tomorrow morning.
Priya (Growth PM): CTA text: A: "Get estimate" B: "Request custom quote". Elaine, can you keep both CTAs short?
Elaine (Content): Yep. Draft CTAs posted: A= "Get estimate" B= "Request custom quote". Popover snippet examples:
- "How is cost calculated?" -> "Tokens x concurrency + reserved discount."
- "Latency differences?" -> "Dedicated tuned for latency; hosted is flexible."
Longer accordion example:
- "Billing details" -> "Monthly estimates include compute + network; reserved commits discount applied post-checkout."
Priya (Growth PM): Nice. Can you also write a tiny microbenchmark line for the compact view: 8 words or less?
Elaine (Content): "p95 latency ~75ms on Dedicated (typical prompts)" (6 words counting numbers).
Sam (UX): Accessibility checklist: aria labels for badges, keyboard ordering, color contrast. Will add alt text for the benchmark blurb.
Alex (Analytics): Also proposing a small UTM suffix: utm_expt=banded_v_full. Will include in links.
Jordan (RevOps): HubSpot: created workflow rules. Variant A enterprise badges map to AE queue, Variant B heavy faq activity -> SDR. Will add canned note templates for AE.
deploy-bot: Experiment flag created: pricing_band_v_full_2026_04_01. Canary rollout scheduled: 2026-04-01T09:00Z.
Priya (Growth PM): Cool. Action items:
- Elaine: final copy for badges, popovers, CTAs (today)
- Marcos/Sam: mock + accessibility tweaks (tomorrow)
- Alex: events + BI view (tomorrow AM)
- Jordan: HubSpot mapping & canned replies (tomorrow)
I'll run a 10-min check 30m after deploy. If tracking gaps appear, @Alex owns triage.
Marcos (Design): Posting initial mocks to the spec doc.
Elaine (Content): Copy uploaded to drive: https://drive.internal/redwood/pricing/badges-draft
Priya (Growth PM): Thanks team :rocket: Let's keep the badge language consumer-friendly and avoid heavy engineering terms. We'll review results at the April growth sync.
Alex (Analytics): Canary rolled to 3% traffic. Smoke test link: https://staging.redwood/pricing?expt=pricing_band_v_full
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: pricing_band_v_full v1 -> 3% traffic. Logs: https://deploys.internal/redwood/logs/2823456789
Priya (Growth PM): Thanks all. Ping here if anything unexpected shows up.
